metais extract — Write the entries the globs select to a directory.

Usage:
  metais extract <package> <glob>... --out <dir> [--overwrite] [--dry-run]
                 [--limit <name>=<value>]... [--json]

Examples:
  metais extract report-1.0.0.metais 'references/**' --out refs
      Writes the package's references into the new directory refs.
  metais extract report-1.0.0.metais references --out refs --dry-run
      Lists the references it would write.
  metais extract report-1.0.0.metais 'templates/**' --out . --overwrite
      Writes the templates into the current directory, replacing the files
      already there.
  metais extract report-1.0.0.metais 'examples/basic/**' --out basic
      Writes the example basic into the new directory basic, to see how the
      package is tested; its inputs are never a real document's data.

Writes every entry any glob selects to <dir>/<entry path>, as stored (metais
help globs). Every glob must select at least one entry, or nothing is written: a
glob that selects nothing is a typo to hear about.

A <dir> that does not exist is created, with its missing parents, and every file
is created beneath it, never through a link. A failed write stops extract, which
lists the files it wrote and removes none of them.

An existing <dir> with no entry at all is written into. One that holds any
entry, a hidden one included, is refused unless --overwrite is given, and then a
file at a path extract writes is replaced, and nothing is deleted: every other
entry is left as it is. Into an existing <dir>, every file is checked before
anything is written, and every refusal is reported together: a link at or above
a file's path, which is never followed, a name that differs only in case from
one extract writes, and a directory or anything else that is not a regular file
where a file goes. An existing file is never read: it is replaced by moving the
new file onto its name. The files are prepared beneath a staging directory,
.metais-staging, inside <dir>, and moved into place; a failure before then
leaves <dir> as it was, and one while moving them lists the files already moved.

--dry-run lists the files extract would write, makes every check, and writes
nothing.

The entries under examples/ are the package's examples. An example is the
author's illustration of the inputs, and of the outputs a render of them should
produce, kept in the package to test it: not your data, and not a preview of
what the package produces, which is a render from generated data with metais
render --sample. An example's inputs are the author's illustration, never a real
document's data: render a real document only from the facts the person supplies,
and without them ask the person for them, never taking them from an example.

Operands:
  <package>
      A packed package file, or a source directory; - is refused, since a
      package is read with random access. Required.
  <glob>
      A glob selecting entries to write. Required.

Flags:
  --out <dir>
      The directory to write into: a new one, or an existing one that is empty,
      or holds entries with --overwrite; required.
  --overwrite
      Write into a <dir> that holds entries, replacing a file at a path extract
      writes; nothing is deleted.
  --dry-run
      List the files extract would write, and write nothing.
  --limit <name>=<value>
      Lower one resource limit for this run, to a whole number no higher than
      its default (a size may end in KiB, MiB or GiB). metais limits lists them.
      May be given more than once.
  --fail-on <severity>
      With warning, a warning fails the command with exit status 1 as an error
      does; no finding's severity changes. Values: error, warning. Default:
      error.
  --json
      Print the result as one JSON document on standard output.
  --color <when>
      Colour human output: auto colours a stream that is a terminal when
      NO_COLOR is unset or empty; always and never override NO_COLOR. Values:
      auto, always, never. Default: auto.
  -h, --help
      Print help to standard output and exit 0; nothing else runs.

Prints:
  The files written, or that would be, each with its size, relative to <dir>.
  With --json, one metais.extract/1 document.

Refusals:
  limit.invalid
      A --limit names no limit, gives a malformed value, or tries to raise one.
      Next: metais limits
  limit.package
      The package breaches one of its limits.
      Next: metais limits
  output.destination.case_variant
      In <dir>, an entry's name differs only in case or normalization from a
      name an entry's path holds.
      Next: metais extract <package> <glob> --out <dir>
  output.destination.commit_failed
      Moving the files into an existing <dir> failed part way; the files already
      moved are listed, and nothing else was changed.
      Next: metais extract <package> <glob> --out <dir>
  output.destination.link
      In <dir>, an entry's path runs through, or ends at, a symbolic link, a
      junction or another reparse point, which is never followed.
      Next: metais extract <package> <glob> --out <dir>
  output.destination.not_directory
      <dir>, or a directory above it, exists and is not a directory; or, in
      <dir>, a file stands where an entry's path needs a directory.
      Next: metais extract <package> <glob> --out <dir>
  output.destination.not_empty
      <dir> holds entries, and --overwrite is not given.
      Next: metais extract <package> <glob> --out <dir> --overwrite
  output.destination.not_regular_file
      In <dir>, a directory, a named pipe, a socket or a device stands at an
      entry's path.
      Next: metais extract <package> <glob> --out <dir>
  output.destination.nothing_written
      A write failed and nothing was left: <dir> could not be created, or, in an
      existing one, a write failed before the commit, another file system is
      mounted inside it, or an entry lies beneath the staging name.
      Next: metais extract <package> <glob> --out <dir>
  output.destination.staging_exists
      An existing <dir> holds .metais-staging, left by a killed write or in use
      by another; nothing is written.
      Next: metais extract <package> <glob> --out <dir>
  output.destination.write_failed
      A write into a new <dir> failed after creating it; the files already
      written are listed and left in place.
      Next: metais extract <package> <glob> --out <dir>
  usage.bad_glob
      A glob does not satisfy the glob grammar.
      Next: metais help globs
  usage.bad_value
      A flag's value is missing, or is not one the flag accepts, or a flag that
      takes no value is given one.
      Next: metais extract --help
  usage.missing_operand
      The package operand is not given.
      Next: metais extract --help
  usage.no_match
      A glob selects no entry; nothing is written.
      Next: metais ls <package> -r
  usage.package_from_stdin
      The package operand is -, standard input.
      Next: metais extract --help
  usage.repeated_flag
      A flag that may be given once is given again.
      Next: metais extract --help
  usage.unexpected_operand
      An operand the command does not take.
      Next: metais extract --help
  usage.unknown_flag
      An argument that is not a flag the command accepts, an abbreviated flag,
      or one-letter aliases written together.
      Next: metais extract --help

  Each line below is a family of codes: how many there are, the cause they share
  and their next step. 'metais help refusals extract' lists every code, and help
  --json gives each code's own cause.

  manifest.* (44)  The manifest breaks one of its rules.
                   Next: metais inspect <package>
  package.* (47)   The package is refused. Next: metais inspect <package>
  schema.* (10)    An input schema is refused. Next: metais inspect <package>
  template.* (9)   An output's path, when or for_each does not parse.
                   Next: metais inspect <package>
